cells.tense: The understanding is complete now, and you are holding it in a live balance.
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: Take an arrangement that already works — hours, trips, what you cover — and count it. Read what the figures say about the blend, shift one band, leave the rest.
cells.core:
You see this whole, and you are holding it steady — not parked, held. A conversation stays honest, a rhythm gets kept, a blend you felt your way into has a shape you could put in a sentence. Done well it looks like adjustment nobody notices: a little more of one thing, a little less of another, and the whole stays lit. Because the picture is finished, you can tell when a stretch is spent and stop it without second-guessing. The balance costs you those small recalibrations, made before anyone asks.

Put a number to one arrangement that's already working — hours, trips, what you cover. Count it out, let the figures say where the blend has drifted, then shift one band and leave the rest alone. Nothing to conclude from it, no verdict on how it's going. Aiming at knowing while you're in the live middle keeps the pen light.

cells.verb: Seeing a whole thing through to where nothing further can be added
cells.place: Inside a flow that will not hold still and is kept steady by hand

cells.tense: You have seen the whole thing, and now you are bracing for where it goes next.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: Catch the first spark of something before you decide what it is. Keep a beginning unaimed for ten minutes — planless, nothing worked out yet — and stop there.
cells.core:
Things show up to you end to end, so you can see where this lands before it gets there, and you are already standing in that. The blend gets over-tightened, small corrections made before the moment that needed them, smoothing against a picture that hasn't shown up. It reads as control, and behind it is a hand that won't wait. What you actually want here is looseness — adjusting to what's here, not to what you have already watched happen. The far side of this is the light kept on without a hand holding it.

Catch the first spark of something before you decide what it is. For ten minutes let a beginning stay unaimed — no plan, no shape, no point settled. It may come to nothing, and that is allowed. Doing this keeps you close to where the adjusting is actually happening.

cells.tense: You had seen the whole of this well before now, and you are still standing at the door of it.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Write one line naming what the thing you already understand is meant to do — not how it will go — and hold it without putting anything into it. The line can wait.
cells.core:
You saw it whole. Much of that has gone quiet — the blend you were tending has gone thin, adjustments made out of habit rather than from the middle, and you are still inside what you understood earlier. Nothing is missing in you. The picture is simply not being used, and the flow is kept with less of you in it than your own read would allow.

Write one line naming what the thing you already understand is meant to do — not how it will go, what it is meant to do. One line only, no plan after it, no date on it. It can sit there until it is needed. A decision held this small is enough to put you back inside a life you have already mapped.

cells.tense: The adjusting is happening through you now and you are not counting it as yours.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Somewhere today, notice a thing newly arrived — not the morning continuing, an actual arrival — and name it once to yourself before you carry on.
cells.core:
Your read is right, and you would say the situation just works. When a rhythm shifts, you are the one already at the new setting; when someone near you needs the blend changed, it has changed before they ask. Something is being done through you and the account you give leaves you out of it. What's operating is a live hand on a living equilibrium, and the hand is yours. Ready to sense the blend and meet what shifts is not a small thing to be doing.

Somewhere today, stop and notice one thing that is newly here — not the morning continuing, an actual arrival. Name it to yourself once and carry on. That's the whole act. Naming the arrival puts you beside it, which is where the adjusting already is. Nothing needs saying to anyone unless you choose it.
